chapters.offline: When it is on its own

scenes.title: Just In Case
scenes.caption: Emergency knowledge, offline.
scenes.narration: There is no signal. How long do you boil creek water?

scenes.caption: First launch. Nothing indexed yet.
scenes.narration: On first launch the library is empty, and the panel says so plainly.

shots.alt: Just In Case on first launch: brand hero, suggested questions, and an empty field library
shots._focusNote:
The scene's evidence is three numbers and a sentence, all in the left rail: the `index empty` pill, INDEX `0 chunks · 0 files`, FIELD LIBRARY `0`, and 'No documents indexed yet. Run the content fetcher or drop PDFs into the sources volume.' At rest they are 8-11px on a 1080-tall canvas — the narration says 'the panel says so plainly' over a panel nobody can read.

h IS 0.5 AND NOT 0.538, ON PURPOSE. The window is square in plate coordinates and its size is set by max(w,h), so h only moves the CENTRE — and the centre matters here because the stage sits above canvas centre by half the caption allowance, which slides the window down about 0.029 of the plate. At h 0.538 the window starts at plate y 0.029 and the status pill (0.021..0.037) is sliced in half; at h 0.5 it starts at 0.010 and the pill is whole. Measured with `ci-video focus-preview`, both values, looking at the pictures.

PULL-BACK, not push-in. This is the film's first screen scene, so it still owes the viewer a wide establishing read of the whole appliance — and it can have both: open full-bleed on the empty panel, then reveal the app around it. It is also the only pull-back in the first half of the film, and a 4.5% default push on the opening screen is the exact 'screenshot being panned' read this pass exists to remove.

LANDSCAPE ONLY. In portrait the drawer is closed on this stage, so the only evidence on the plate is the `Index empty` pill at the very top — 2% of the frame, and portrait's tightest honoured window is 73.8%, which does not get near it. A format left out keeps the legacy move rather than pretending.

scenes.caption: Copy documents in. Ingestion indexes them.
scenes.narration: Copy reference documents into the sources volume. Ingestion indexes them.

shots.alt: The field library sidebar listing thirty-two indexed documents grouped by category
shots._focusNote:
The same rectangle as `welcome-empty`, deliberately: these two scenes are a before/after of one panel, and framing them identically is what turns `0 chunks · 0 files` into `11,490 chunks · 32 files` and `index empty` into `Ready · 32 docs` as a comparison the viewer can actually make. Different framings would have made it two unrelated shots.

Same reason for h 0.5 — see the note on `welcome-empty`. At h 0.538 the caption-allowance offset slides the window down and halves the `Ready · 32 docs` pill, which is one of the two things this caption claims.

DRIFT-DOWN keeps its authored motion and now has something to travel through. A drift STARTS at the focus, so `ci-video focus-preview --scene field-library --at start` is the frame that has to be checked: window 0.010..0.548, pill whole, `11,490 chunks · 32 files` legible. The `--at end` frame is 0.073..0.611 — the pill has scrolled off the top and four filenames have arrived at the bottom, which is the move doing its job. The full 0.063 of travel was taken, so this is not the headroom-starved case that renders dead still while the storyboard claims it moves.

LANDSCAPE ONLY: in portrait the drawer opens full-bleed and the panel is already large.

scenes.caption: Eight categories. Medicine, water, power, food, comms.
scenes.narration: The whole shelf stays browsable offline, on hardware you own.

shots.alt: The field library scrolled past its first categories, showing later category headers and their reference filenames with per-document chunk counts
shots._focusNote:
The caption has always said 'Eight categories, thirty-two documents' while the category headers sat at ~10px on a 1080-tall canvas — the claim was in the words and not in the picture. This lands on the shelf itself so SURVIVAL & PREPAREDNESS, ENGINEERING & WATER and their neighbours are legible, which is the whole point of a scene about breadth.

0.54 square because that is the tightest the kit will honour: MAX_SCALE is 2.4 and the window is square in normalised coordinates, so anything smaller clamps and the framing stops being mine. Measured with `ci-video focus-preview`, not guessed.

LANDSCAPE ONLY — in portrait the drawer is already full-bleed.

scenes._transitionNote: The one place in this film where a cut is punctuation rather than damage control. It is the chapter boundary — `first-run` ends and `ask` begins — and the film had no cut at any chapter boundary at all: both existing cuts (`check-the-sources`, `no-network`) are there to stop a double-exposure ghost, so the grammar was being used only as a repair and never as an edit. The subject changes hard here too: the scene before ends full-bleed on the shelf's category headers, this one opens wide on the composer end of the app.
scenes.caption: Water, burns, wounds, solar wiring, food — before you type a word.
scenes.narration: First aid, power, water, food. The suggestions come from the shelf itself.

shots.alt: The six suggested questions the app offers on a ready appliance — purifying water, first aid for a burn, a seventy-two hour kit, treating a wound, wiring a solar panel to a battery, and preserving food without refrigeration
shots._shotNote:
These are the app's OWN suggestions (SUGGESTED_PROMPTS, public/app.js), not a list written for the video. That is the point: the breadth on screen is breadth the product actually has, and it moves when the product moves.

The corpus does NOT cover vehicle transportation, and device repair only through the iFixit ZIM — which is `_ftindex:no`, so it is browsable but cannot be retrieved from. Neither is claimed here, in the caption or the narration.
shots._focusNote:
RETARGETED — the rectangle this shot carried framed no chips at all. It was (0.171, 0.211), which resolves to a window over plate y 0.303..0.841 while both chip rows sit at 0.821..0.886. `ci-video focus-preview --scene what-you-can-ask` reconstructs the end frame as an empty dark rectangle with the chips sliced off along the bottom edge, under the caption band, i.e. the caption enumerated five subjects over a frame containing none of them. The prose note that used to sit here described a 0.65-wide rectangle at y 0.35; the numbers beside it were 0.538 at 0.211, so the note and the value had come apart at some point and the note was the thing being read.

The chip block is x 0.337..0.808 by y 0.821..0.886 — 0.47 on its longer side, under the 0.538 landscape floor, so 0.538 square is the tightest available and the shape of the block cannot be honoured. x 0.303 centres that square on the block (0.035 of margin left, 0.032 right, so no chip is clipped at either end — the clipped-'H' failure the old note describes is avoided by centring, not by widening).

y 0.462 IS THE MAXIMUM the plate allows: y + h must stay inside the screenshot, so the window is bottom-anchored at 0.462..1.0. That is also the only placement that clears the caption band — the chips land at 0.69 and 0.76 of canvas height and the band starts at ~0.85. Anything higher pushes the second row under the caption.

PUSH-IN, changed from drift-down, and forced: a bottom-anchored focus has zero headroomDown, so drift-down would hit the degradation path in cameraMove and silently become a push anyway. Declaring the push is honest, and it is the better move regardless — the shot opens wide and ends with the six questions filling the frame at the moment the cursor picks one.
shots._pointerNote:
The chip 'How do I purify water in the field?' — a real control, the app's own SUGGESTED_PROMPTS button, and the first subject the caption names ('Water'). Clicking it is also the film's argument: you can ask this thing without typing.

LANDSCAPE (0.400, 0.840): inside the pill, which spans x 0.337..0.482 by y 0.821..0.847 on the committed plate. Left of the pill's centre and low in it on purpose — the arrow's hotspot is its tip and its body hangs down-right, so this puts the body across the pill's lower edge instead of across the words. Inside the focus window (0.302..0.840 x 0.461..0.999), so the cursor is on canvas for the whole push rather than sliding off the end of it.

PORTRAIT (0.288, 0.830): the same chip on the mobile plate, where it spans x 0.032..0.545 by y 0.815..0.845. Centred, because a phone frame gets a tap ripple and a ripple has no body to keep off the label.

Both measured off the committed PNGs at 0.05 gridding, not derived from the landscape numbers — the app is responsive and the chip is 51% of the width on mobile against 15% on desktop.

scenes._prosodyNote:
Pinned NEUTRAL to match the eleven tracks already in this film. Kit 0.14.0 introduced per-kind default prosody, and 0.15.0 reports that every existing recording here was made before it — so a new line taking the new default would be the only one in the cut read at a different rate. The kit calls that acceptable and it is probably inaudible at -3%, but a film carrying two registers is a worse defect than a film carrying one slightly stale one.

Adopting the new register is a real improvement and should happen — as `ci-video narrate --restyle` across all twelve lines, in its own change, where the re-recorded audio can be verified as a set. Not smuggled in under a content edit.
scenes._captionNote: Names ONLY what is in this frame. The first version read 'Burns, wounds, solar wiring, canning, radio, navigation' — and radio and navigation appear in no chip on screen. The shelf does carry ARRL Emergency Comms and FM3-25-26 Map Reading, so the words were true of the PRODUCT and false of the PICTURE, which is the exact defect the fleet review named when it warned not to let a count migrate into a caption. Caught by reading the rendered caption band, not the storyboard.

scenes.caption: Type your own. The question never leaves the machine.
scenes.narration: Type any question in plain language; nothing leaves the device to answer it.

shots.alt: A question of the viewer's own — how long to boil creek water — typed into the composer, with the suggested-question chips still offered above it
shots._altNote: No count here, deliberately. The app renders six chips at desktop width and three at portrait — `.chip-extra { display: none }` under 620px — so one alt string cannot name a number that is true of both plates, and this one is read against both. Verified in the 9:16 cut: three chips.
shots._pointerNote:
The composer. The caption is 'Type your own' and the narration is 'Type any question in plain language', so the named control is the field — and this plate is the one that has a question sitting in it. A cursor arriving at the field, settling and clicking is the beat.

LANDSCAPE (0.600, 0.925): inside the input, which spans x 0.337..0.795 by y 0.898..0.955. Placed past the end of the typed text (which stops at x 0.545) so the arrow does not sit on top of the sentence the shot exists to show — a click into the empty part of a field is where a caret goes anyway. x is under 0.62, which is the threshold at which pointer.mjs flips the approach direction, so the arrow enters from the right and travels left across the field: the correct read for a cursor arriving at something.

PORTRAIT (0.760, 0.930): the mobile input spans x 0.028..0.865 by y 0.902..0.958 and the typed text stops at 0.68, so this is the same idea on the phone plate — clear of the words, well inside the field, and clear of the Send button at 0.885..0.975.
shots._focusNote:
NO FOCUS IN EITHER FORMAT, and this one is a measured refusal rather than an omission.

The subject is the composer at plate y 0.898..0.955 — the bottom 7% of the screenshot. A focus move ends with the frame full-bleed and the plate's bottom edge no further up than the canvas bottom, so anything in that last 7% lands in the bottom 13% of the canvas. The caption band starts at ~0.85. Solving for a window that puts the typed question above it needs a window under 0.47 of the plate; the landscape floor is 0.538. There is no rectangle. Checked with `ci-video focus-preview` at the bottom-anchored (0.326, 0.462): the reconstruction puts 'How long do I boil creek water to make it safe?' directly under the band marker.

So the shot stays wide and the cursor carries it. That is the honest split: the camera has nothing to say about this beat and the pointer has everything.

fill: How long do I boil creek water to make it safe?

scenes.caption: Retrieval finds the passages. A local model writes the answer.
scenes.narration: Ask a question. Retrieval finds the passages, and a model on this device answers.

shots.alt: The typed question — how long to boil creek water — asked and answered in the chat, with a collapsed sources accordion
shots._focusNote:
The film's first punch-in, and it arrives late on purpose: four earlier scenes are this same app shell, so the wide read is long since established and this scene can spend its dwell on the conversation instead of re-introducing the furniture. It ends on the question, the answer and the collapsed SOURCES row — the narration, line for line.

The 16:9 window is always SQUARE in normalised image coordinates, because the capture and the canvas are both 16:9. So the only lever a landscape rectangle has is its longer side: scale = 1.263 / max(w, h), clamped to [1.263, 2.4]. max here is 0.65, giving 1.943x. An earlier attempt pointed at the answer bubble alone (0.51) was therefore pointless — it asks for 2.48x, clamps to 2.4, and the extra 0.14 of window it wins slices the question bubble instead.

Portrait is a different instrument. The mobile capture is already legible at rest, and its window is square-ish too, so any tight crop slices full-width body copy — there is no honest close-up available. What IS available is the reframe coverScale gives for free: w 1.0 asks for nothing tighter than full-bleed, the phone frame drops away and the screen grows 39%. That is the portrait shot-size change; a portrait crop is not.

fill: How long do I boil creek water to make it safe?

scenes._transitionNote: Forced by the focus on the scene before it, and measured rather than assumed. Both scenes now end full-bleed on the same app screen at nearly the same scale, and the default half-second cross-dissolve between them renders as two full-frame copies of the answer text sliding through each other — a screenful of overlapping body copy that reads as a broken render, not a transition. At rest the same dissolve was harmless, because both plates were small cards on a lot of empty ground. AUTHORING.md predicts this ('a cross-dissolve between two shots of the SAME app screen reads as a double-exposure ghost'); punching in is what makes it unmissable. Cut instead — which is also the right edit, since this is the escalation from the answer to its receipts.
scenes.caption: Every answer opens onto the documents behind it.
scenes.narration: See exactly which documents the answer came from. Verify before you act.

shots.alt: The expanded sources accordion listing the documents the answer was drawn from — two field manuals and, marked as encyclopedia, a Wikipedia article served from the offline ZIM library — each with the passage that matched
shots._focusNote:
The credibility beat, and the one frame in this film that is genuinely unreadable wide: the filenames the caption promises — 100_Survival/FM21-76-US-Army-Survival.pdf and the two engineering handbooks — are about 13px on a 1080-tall canvas at rest. At 1.974x they are 26px and the claim is verifiable rather than asserted.

drift-down rather than push-in, and it has room: headroomDown is 100px against a 107px request, so the shot travels 0.063 of the plate down through the three cards instead of stalling. That matters — a focus that lands hard against the coverage clamp leaves drift-down with nowhere to go and renders DEAD STILL while the storyboard claims it moves. Worth re-checking with the kit's own focusState after any change to this rectangle.

LANDSCAPE ONLY, deliberately. On mobile the source list is full-bleed body copy that is already comfortable to read, so the only portrait framing available would crop the card text at the sides. A format left out keeps the legacy move, which is the right answer here: 'this screen does not need a camera on 9:16' should render as a plain shot, not a confidently wrong one.
shots._pointerNote:
The SOURCES disclosure. The caption says the answer 'opens onto the documents behind it' and the narration says 'See exactly which documents' — the control that does the opening is `details.sources > summary`, and this shot's own capture script clicks it. Pointing at it is the film showing the click it already performed off-screen.

LANDSCAPE (0.3455, 0.421): on the ▾ triangle, which sits at x 0.3435..0.3475 with the row's text centred on y 0.4245. The tip goes on the triangle rather than on the word SOURCES so the arrow's body falls into the gap before the label instead of across it. Inside the focus window (0.227..0.765 x 0.195..0.733), so the cursor tracks the drift instead of leaving frame.

PORTRAIT (0.120, 0.4445): the same row on the mobile plate, where the triangle is at x 0.065 and SOURCES runs 0.083..0.200. The tap ripple is centred between them; its radius is 7.5% of the screen width, which at x 0.12 stays clear of the left edge.

The accordion is already open on this plate, so the press reads as 'this row is the thing you open' rather than as a state change — which is what the caption claims and all it claims.

fill: How long do I boil creek water to make it safe?

scenes._transitionNote: Same reason check-the-sources cuts: the scene before it ends full-bleed on this very app screen at nearly the same scale, and a half-second cross-dissolve between two shots of the SAME screen renders as a double-exposure ghost of overlapping body copy rather than as a transition. AUTHORING.md predicts it; the focus on the outgoing scene is what makes it unmissable.
scenes.caption: No connection. Wikipedia, on the box, in the answers.
scenes.narration: The network is gone and nothing changes. The encyclopedia is on the box too.

shots.alt: The appliance with a ZIM library mounted: the System panel reads Encyclopedia, three archives, beside the local index, and the sidebar footer reads Runs 100% offline
shots._shotNote: Captured with EVERY external request blocked and recorded — see the egress guard in capture.config.mjs. If this app ever fetches a font, a script or a beacon, the capture fails instead of quietly filming a product that phones home under a narration saying it does not. The offline claim in this film is enforced, not asserted.
shots._focusNote:
Lands on the System panel, where the two facts this scene asserts are actually written: ENCYCLOPEDIA / 3 archives, and the footer's offline dot. At rest they are ~11px on a 1080-tall canvas — legible on a desktop monitor, not in a 16:9 video.

0.54 SQUARE IS DELIBERATE, and was measured with `ci-video focus-preview` rather than guessed. An earlier 0.42x0.50 asked for scale 3.0, clamped to the 2.4 ceiling, and past the ceiling the rectangle stops being read at all — moving its centre changes nothing, so the framing was the kit's rather than mine. 0.54 gives the same picture at scale 2.34, under control, and leaves the window free to sit against the left canvas edge where the sidebar is.

LANDSCAPE ONLY. In portrait the sidebar is off-canvas below 920px (style.css) and the drawer eval opens it full-bleed, so the panel is already large and a crop would only slice it. A format left out keeps the legacy move, which is the right answer when a screen does not need a camera on 9:16.

scenes._transitionNote: Two reasons, one of them measured. The subject changes hard — the scene before is about the network being gone while everything still works, this one is about the language model being absent, a different failure and a different panel. And with this scene now opening full-bleed on the banner while `no-network` ends full-bleed on the System panel, the default half-second dissolve would cross two copies of the same app screen at nearly the same scale: the double-exposure ghost AUTHORING.md names, and the same one that already forced cuts on `check-the-sources` and `no-network`. Changing the motion here is what created the hazard, so the cut goes in with it rather than after somebody screenshots it.
scenes.caption: No model on the box? It says so, and keeps going.
scenes.narration: With no language model installed it says so, and the library stays browsable.

shots.alt: The degraded state: an LLM missing status pill and a banner naming the directory the model files belong in
shots._focusNote:
PULL-BACK IS THE CAPTION. 'It says so, and keeps going' is two beats in order: open on the thing that says so — the `LLM missing` pill and the banner naming /app/gguf_models — then pull back to the appliance with its thirty-two documents still listed underneath. A push-in would have run the sentence backwards.

LANDSCAPE 0.62 wide, not the 0.538 floor, because the banner runs x 0.203..0.813 and a 0.538 window slices it mid-sentence. Half a sentence in frame is worse than 13% less magnification, and the whole point of the shot is that the app tells you what to do. x 0.195 puts the window at 0.194..0.814 — both ends of the banner inside it with a pixel to spare. h 0.58 is doing the same job h 0.5 does on `welcome-empty`: it only moves the window's centre, and at 0.58 the window starts at plate 0.014 so the status pill (0.021..0.045) is whole rather than sliced by the caption-allowance offset. scale lands at 2.081, honoured exactly, no clamp. Verified with `ci-video focus-preview`.

PORTRAIT w 1.0 asks for nothing tighter than full-bleed, which is the only thing worth asking for on this plate: the banner wraps to three lines running x 0.02..0.95, so any window narrower than the plate cuts words off both ends, and portrait's floor is 73.8%. What the declaration buys is the coverScale reframe the `answer` shot uses — the phone frame drops away and the screen grows 39%, which is the whole legibility gain available here. h 0.62 keeps the centre high so the window anchors to the top of the plate where the banner is.

scenes.title: Runs on your hardware
scenes.caption: One Docker stack. No accounts, no cloud.
scenes.narration: Your documents, your questions, your answers. It keeps working when the network does not.
scenes._narrationNote: The line used to be "One Docker stack. No accounts, no cloud. It keeps working when the network does not." — whose first seven words were the caption, verbatim, read aloud while the caption was on screen. The voice now spends that time on the only thing this scene has left to say. The three nouns are the film's own arc in order — the shelf, the typed question, the cited answer — so the recap recaps something the viewer watched rather than introducing a fourth claim in the last six seconds.
scenes._itemsNote:
MESSAGING.md's "ownership tally". `Monthly fee - $0` gave up its slot to `Encyclopedia - On disk` when the ZIM library landed: four chips fit one landscape row and five wrap, and of the five candidates the price is the one the outro's own argument already implies while the encyclopedia is a capability the viewer has just watched being cited.

`Data leaves home - Never` is a claim, so it was verified rather than assumed, because the fleet review caught this exact chip being false on Spellbook. CMakeLists.txt defaults JIC_SENTRY OFF, the Dockerfile defaults ARG JIC_SENTRY=0 and in that state links no Sentry code at all, and docker-publish.yml passes no build-args. It is now ALSO enforced at capture time by the egress guard in video/capture.config.mjs.

scenes.narration: Just In Case, from Companion Intelligence. UnCloud your life.
